subject: AI & Agents
title: New Jobs AI Creates
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on New Jobs AI Creates.

hook.text: Prompt engineer, AI ethicist, synthetic data curator — these jobs didn't exist three years ago.

buildup.text: Every transformative technology destroys old jobs while creating entirely new categories.

discovery.text: AI needs human oversight: trainers, evaluators, bias auditors, and safety researchers.

twist.text: The fastest-growing AI jobs often require liberal arts skills — communication, ethics, and critical thinking.

climax.text: Companies are hiring more AI-adjacent roles than AI is eliminating traditional roles, so far.

punchline.text: AI destroys job descriptions. Humans write new ones.

quiz.question: What types of skills do many new AI-related jobs require?
options: Communication, ethics, and critical thinking from liberal arts
Only advanced mathematics and computer science

details.summary: While AI threatens some jobs, it also creates entirely new roles: prompt engineers, AI trainers, alignment researchers, data curators, and AI-human interaction designers among them.
details.whyItMatters: Focusing only on job losses misses the full picture. Understanding emerging roles helps workers and educators prepare for the jobs AI is creating alongside the ones it displaces.
takeaways: AI is creating new job categories that did not exist before
Prompt engineering and AI training are growing career fields
The net employment effect of AI remains uncertain

faq.question: What new jobs has AI created?
faq.answer: Prominent new roles include prompt engineers, AI safety researchers, data labelers, AI ethicists, model fine-tuners, retrieval-augmented generation specialists, and AI integration consultants.

faq.question: Will AI create enough jobs to replace the ones it eliminates?
faq.answer: Historically, technology waves create more jobs than they destroy, but the transition is painful. The speed of AI adoption may exceed the speed at which displaced workers can retrain.
